apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway
---

kind: ConfigMap

    }

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests practical skills in implementing controlled, observable deployments in a multi-tenant CNF gateway environment. It checks familiarity with canary strategies, per-tenant isolation, and metric-driven promotion/rollback.

## Key Concepts

- Canary deployments with Argo Rollouts
- Per-tenant traffic shaping and isolation
- Prometheus-based SLIs and analysis templates
- Automated rollback and promotion thresholds
- End-to-end testing in a single-tenant namespace before broader rollout

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Rollout
metadata:
  name: gateway-rollout-tenant-a
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gateway
      tenant: a
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gateway
        tenant: a
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: registry.example.com/cnf/gateway:latest
  strategy:
    canary:
      steps:
      - setWeight: 10
      - pause: { duration: 5m }
      - setWeight: 100
      analysis:
        templates:
        - templateName: canary-metrics
        metrics:
        - name: latency
          interval: 30s
          successCondition: result < 0.001 * 0.15
        - name: error-rate
          interval: 30s
          successCondition: result < 0.005
```

```yaml
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: AnalysisTemplate
metadata:
  name: canary-metrics
spec:
  metrics:
  - name: latency
    provider:
      prometheus:
        url: http://prometheus.k8s.svc
        query: sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_sum[5m])) / sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_count[5m]))
  - name: error-rate
    provider:
      prometheus:
        url: http://prometheus.k8s.svc
        query: sum(rate(http_requests_total{status!~"2.."}[5m]))
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you adapt this for cross-cluster canaries?
- What monitoring dashboards would you expose to operators for this flow?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of per-tenant feature flags, sidecar traffic manipulation, and config management in Kubernetes. It also exercises practical routing logic and isolation between tenants. 

## Key Concepts
- Namespace ConfigMap per-tenant feature flags
- Sidecar-based request rewriting for canary paths
- Tenant isolation via X-TENANT-ID header
- Minimal manifests for quick end-to-end validation
- Safe defaults when feature flag is off

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConfigMap example
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: cnf.canary
  namespace: tenant-a
data:
  enabled: "true"
  target: "/v1/foo"
```
```yaml
# Sidecar snippet (pseudo)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: cnf-sidecar
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: sidecar
        image: cnf/sidecar:latest
        env:
        - name: CANARY_ENABLED
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: cnf.canary
              key: enabled
        - name: CANARY_TARGET
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: cnf.canary
              key: target
```

- What are potential race conditions with ConfigMap updates and how would you mitigate them?
